discovery_method_tests.method: Pearson chi-square test of independence; Cramer's V effect size.

with_temp.interpretation_note: Pearson chi-square asymptotic assumptions are not met under the common heuristic; do not overinterpret the p-value. Rare discovery categories were retained, not pooled.

without_temp.interpretation_note: Pearson chi-square asymptotic assumptions are not met under the common heuristic; do not overinterpret the p-value. Rare discovery categories were retained, not pooled.

discovery_method_tests.caveat: Discovery techniques have different detection sensitivities and survey selection effects. The confirmed-planet catalogue is not an unbiased sample of all planetary systems. An association does not show that discovery method causes physical properties or cluster membership.

temperature_comparison.interpretation: Partition sensitivity to temperature inclusion, not a causal effect.

recommendation.recommendation: Retain K=4 as an exploratory candidate, but defer freezing it as the primary scientific configuration pending review of the K=2/3 simplicity advantage, K=5 refinement, feature overlap, temperature sensitivity, and catalogue selection effects.

limitations: K-means partitions are geometric groupings, not established astronomical classes.
Silhouette is not a scientific validation metric by itself.
One-dimensional overlap coefficients are approximate and depend on the shared binning scheme.
Discovery methods have different sensitivities and survey selection effects; the confirmed catalogue is not an unbiased system sample.
No causal inference is supported by discovery-method associations.
Planet-level validation does not model dependence among planets around a shared host star.
